scope: two-level cumulative direct-repair fraction boundaries 0 and 1

source.interpretation: DIRPF is an accumulated direct-repair capability at each station. A failed item's complexity is drawn once; if above the base threshold, the item travels to the next support level. The top level has capability 1.0.

model_delta.common: E05 plus E04's BASE-01 to DEPOT-01 support row and depot station; retain E05 local stock 1, add depot stock 0 and depot ItemRepair DIRPF 1, DIRPT 1 hour; retain 2-hour upward/downward transport.
model_delta.sole_arm_difference: BASE-01 ItemRepair DIRPF 1.0 in local arm, 0.0 in upstream arm; all other rows except descriptive PDESC identical.

predeclared_native_acceptance: Both frozen inputs import and export all populated business rows exactly, convert with zero errors, calculate, and produce nonempty event and JSON reports under guarded session-0 SSH.

The local arm routes removed LRUs to BASE-01 ItemRepair; the upstream arm routes them to DEPOT-01 across the accepted two-hour upward support link. Trace physical item identities, stock, repair timing, mission and system impact for every observed demand.

All native steps exit zero; raw artifacts, invocation and source closure are hashed; 72 half-hour report intervals and terminal quantities reconcile with events; a separate reviewer replays assertions read-only.
limits: Boundary fractions demonstrate deterministic station routing under one fixed seed. Intermediate accumulated fractions require a separate native sample panel and are not accepted by this scope.
Partial discard, SURPF, CMF, PRU/DU categories, multiple bases, GUI visual behavior and cross-engine equivalence are outside this scope.
